stem: A finance clerk can both create a new vendor and approve payments to that vendor. Which control BEST addresses the fraud risk this creates?

options.text: Separation of duties
options.rationale: Separation of duties splits conflicting responsibilities (creating vendors vs approving payments) so no single person can commit and conceal fraud.

options.text: Mandatory vacation only
options.rationale: Mandatory vacation helps detect ongoing fraud but does not prevent one person from holding both conflicting duties.

options.text: Longer passwords
options.rationale: Password strength is unrelated to the conflict-of-duties problem described.

options.text: Full-disk encryption
options.rationale: Encryption protects data at rest, not the separation of conflicting job functions.

stem: Which personnel control MOST helps detect fraud and reduce dependence on a single individual by periodically moving staff between roles?

options.text: Job rotation
options.rationale: Rotating employees exposes irregularities left by predecessors and reduces single-person dependency and collusion opportunity.

options.text: Non-disclosure agreement
options.rationale: An NDA restricts information sharing; it does not rotate duties or detect fraud.

options.text: Security awareness poster
options.rationale: Awareness posters educate but do not provide the detective/deterrent effect of rotating roles.

options.text: Clean desk policy
options.rationale: A clean desk policy protects physical information exposure, not role dependency or fraud detection.

stem: A bank requires employees in sensitive roles to take at least one continuous week of vacation each year. What is the PRIMARY security purpose?

options.text: To detect fraud or irregularities that surface when someone else covers the role
options.rationale: Mandatory vacation forces another person to perform the duties, exposing hidden fraud that requires the perpetrator's continuous presence to conceal.

options.text: To improve employee morale exclusively
options.rationale: Morale is a side benefit; the security purpose is fraud detection.

options.text: To reduce payroll costs
options.rationale: Mandatory paid vacation does not reduce payroll costs and that is not its security aim.

options.text: To comply with encryption standards
options.rationale: Vacation policy has nothing to do with encryption standards.

stem: Before granting a new hire access to sensitive systems, what should generally occur FIRST as part of personnel security?

options.text: Complete background screening appropriate to the role's sensitivity
options.rationale: Pre-employment/background screening proportional to role sensitivity should precede granting access to sensitive systems.

options.text: Give full administrative access on day one to speed onboarding
options.rationale: Granting broad access before screening violates least privilege and personnel-security practice.

options.text: Schedule the employee's exit interview
options.rationale: Exit interviews occur at termination, not before onboarding access.

options.text: Assign the employee to lead the audit committee
options.rationale: Role assignment of that nature is irrelevant to pre-access screening.

stem: An employee is being involuntarily terminated for cause. Regarding system access, what should happen FIRST/at the moment of termination?

options.text: Disable the employee's accounts and revoke access promptly, coordinated with the termination meeting
options.rationale: For involuntary terminations, access should be revoked at (or just before) the termination notification to prevent retaliatory misuse.

options.text: Leave access active for two weeks as a courtesy
options.rationale: Leaving a for-cause terminee's access active invites sabotage or data theft.

options.text: Announce the termination publicly before revoking access
options.rationale: Publicizing before revoking access gives the individual time and motive to misuse still-active accounts.

options.text: Wait until the next quarterly access review
options.rationale: Delaying revocation to a periodic review leaves a dangerous window open.

stem: A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) is primarily used to accomplish which of the following?

options.text: Legally bind an individual to protect confidential information
options.rationale: An NDA contractually obligates the signer to keep specified confidential information private.

options.text: Grant the employee unlimited system privileges
options.rationale: An NDA restricts disclosure; it does not grant access privileges.

options.text: Replace the need for access controls
options.rationale: An NDA is a legal control, not a substitute for technical access controls.

options.text: Serve as a data backup mechanism
options.rationale: An NDA has nothing to do with data backup.

stem: When an employee changes departments, their old access is never removed, accumulating over years. This problem is MOST accurately called what, and which principle is violated?

options.text: Privilege creep, violating least privilege
options.rationale: Accumulating unneeded access across role changes is 'privilege creep,' which violates least privilege.

options.text: Separation of duties, which is strengthened
options.rationale: Accumulated access weakens, not strengthens, control and is unrelated to separation of duties being improved.

options.text: Defense in depth, which is satisfied
options.rationale: Excess access does not satisfy defense in depth; it increases attack surface.

options.text: Mandatory vacation, which is enforced
options.rationale: This scenario concerns access accumulation, not vacation policy.

stem: Separation of duties is in place, but two employees could still commit fraud by working together. Which additional control BEST reduces this collusion risk?

options.text: Job rotation and mandatory vacation to disrupt sustained collusion
options.rationale: Rotating roles and forcing absences make sustained collusion harder to maintain and easier to detect, complementing separation of duties.

options.text: Removing all separation of duties
options.rationale: Removing separation of duties makes single-person fraud easier and worsens the situation.

options.text: Giving both employees identical unrestricted access
options.rationale: Identical unrestricted access removes controls and increases fraud opportunity.

options.text: Disabling all logging
options.rationale: Disabling logging eliminates detection capability, aiding rather than reducing collusion.

stem: A vendor's contractors will access internal systems. Which personnel-security measure is MOST important to apply to them?

options.text: Contractually require screening, NDAs, and access aligned to least privilege for the contractors
options.rationale: Third-party staff should be held to equivalent personnel-security controls (screening, NDAs, least-privilege access) via contract to manage the risk they introduce.

options.text: Assume the vendor handled everything and apply no controls
options.rationale: Blind trust in the vendor leaves the organization exposed to unvetted access.

options.text: Grant contractors domain administrator rights for convenience
options.rationale: Excessive privilege to external contractors dramatically increases risk.

options.text: Skip NDAs because they are external
options.rationale: External parties especially need NDAs to bind them to confidentiality.

stem: During onboarding, which document BEST sets expectations for how an employee may use company systems?

options.text: An acceptable use policy (AUP) acknowledgment
options.rationale: The AUP defines acceptable/prohibited use of company systems, and acknowledging it sets clear expectations at onboarding.

options.text: The company's product roadmap
options.rationale: A product roadmap does not govern acceptable system use.

options.text: A vendor purchase order
options.rationale: A purchase order is a procurement document, unrelated to use expectations.

options.text: The office floor plan
options.rationale: A floor plan does not set system-use expectations.

subtopicTag: Least Privilege vs Need to Know
stem: An analyst has clearance to a classification level but is denied access to a specific project's data at that level. Which principle MOST directly justifies the denial?

options.text: Need to know
options.rationale: Clearance grants eligibility, but need-to-know restricts access to only the specific information required for one's duties, justifying the denial.

options.text: Mandatory vacation
options.rationale: Mandatory vacation is a fraud-detection control, irrelevant to information access scope.

options.text: Job rotation
options.rationale: Job rotation concerns moving staff between roles, not access scoping by need-to-know.

options.text: Defense in depth
options.rationale: Defense in depth is a layered-control concept, not the specific principle limiting access to what one needs.

stem: To ensure consistent, complete removal of access and assets when employees leave, what is the BEST practice?

options.text: Use a standardized offboarding checklist covering access revocation, asset return, and knowledge transfer
options.rationale: A standardized checklist ensures every departure consistently revokes access, recovers assets, and transfers knowledge, closing gaps.

options.text: Handle each departure ad hoc based on who remembers what
options.rationale: Ad hoc offboarding leads to missed accounts and unreturned assets.

options.text: Only revoke email but leave other systems active
options.rationale: Partial revocation leaves exploitable residual access.

options.text: Do nothing until the annual audit finds leftover accounts
options.rationale: Waiting for an annual audit leaves dangerous orphaned access for months.

stem: Which factor MOST appropriately determines the depth of a pre-employment background check?

options.text: The sensitivity and privileges of the role being filled
options.rationale: Screening depth should be proportional to role sensitivity/access — higher-privilege roles warrant deeper checks.

options.text: The candidate's astrological sign
options.rationale: This is irrelevant and discriminatory, not a valid basis.

options.text: The color of the candidate's résumé paper
options.rationale: Superficial factors have no bearing on screening depth.

options.text: How quickly the manager wants to fill the seat
options.rationale: Urgency should not compromise appropriate screening for sensitive roles.

stem: A highly sensitive operation (e.g., issuing a root cryptographic key) must require two authorized individuals acting together. This control is BEST known as what?

options.text: Dual control / two-person integrity
options.rationale: Dual control (two-person integrity) requires two authorized people to jointly perform a highly sensitive action, preventing unilateral misuse.

options.text: Job rotation
options.rationale: Job rotation moves people between roles over time; it does not require two people to act simultaneously.

options.text: Mandatory vacation
options.rationale: Mandatory vacation is a periodic fraud-detection control, not a simultaneous two-person requirement.

options.text: Single sign-on
options.rationale: SSO is an authentication convenience, unrelated to requiring two people for one action.

stem: An employee transfers from finance to marketing. To uphold least privilege, what should happen FIRST regarding their access?

options.text: Review and remove access no longer needed for the new role before granting new access
options.rationale: On transfer, obsolete access should be reviewed and revoked (preventing privilege creep) as new role-appropriate access is provisioned.

options.text: Keep all finance access and simply add marketing access
options.rationale: Retaining old access while adding new causes privilege creep, violating least privilege.

options.text: Remove all access permanently and never restore any
options.rationale: The employee still needs role-appropriate access; removing everything without provisioning the new role blocks their work.

options.text: Do nothing since they are still an employee
options.rationale: Role change requires access review; inaction leaves inappropriate finance access in place.

stem: Separation of duties is best defined as which of the following?

options.text: Dividing a critical task so that no single person can complete it alone
options.rationale: Separation of duties splits a sensitive process among multiple people so no individual controls it end to end.

options.text: Requiring employees to take annual vacations
options.rationale: That describes mandatory vacation, a distinct control.

options.text: Rotating employees through different jobs
options.rationale: That describes job rotation, not separation of duties.

options.text: Encrypting all sensitive data at rest
options.rationale: That is a data-protection control unrelated to dividing duties.

stem: A privileged employee suddenly downloads massive volumes of data unrelated to their job just before resigning. What is the BEST personnel-security-informed response?

options.text: Treat it as a potential insider threat: preserve evidence, restrict access, and involve HR/legal/security
options.rationale: Anomalous bulk access before departure is a classic insider-threat indicator warranting evidence preservation and coordinated HR/legal/security response.

options.text: Ignore it because the person is leaving anyway
options.rationale: Departure increases, not decreases, insider-exfiltration risk; ignoring it invites data theft.

options.text: Publicly accuse the employee immediately
options.rationale: Premature public accusation risks defamation and may tip off the individual to destroy evidence.

options.text: Grant additional access to observe what else they take
options.rationale: Expanding access to a suspected insider is reckless and increases potential damage.

stem: Embedding security responsibilities directly into job descriptions MOST directly supports which outcome?

options.text: Clear accountability, so employees know their security obligations as part of their role
options.rationale: Documenting security duties in job descriptions establishes accountability and sets expectations from the outset.

options.text: Elimination of the need for any technical controls
options.rationale: Documenting responsibilities complements, not replaces, technical controls.

options.text: Guaranteed prevention of all insider threats
options.rationale: No single measure guarantees prevention of insider threats.

options.text: Reduced need to pay employees
options.rationale: This has no relationship to compensation.

stem: A contract with a third-party service provider ends. Regarding the provider's access to your systems and data, what should happen FIRST?

options.text: Revoke the provider's access and confirm return/destruction of your data per contract
options.rationale: At contract end, promptly revoke provider access and ensure data is returned or securely destroyed as the agreement requires.

options.text: Leave the provider's credentials active indefinitely
options.rationale: Leaving former-vendor credentials active is a serious unmanaged access risk.

options.text: Assume the provider will delete data without any verification
options.rationale: Unverified assumptions about data destruction leave the organization exposed and non-compliant.

options.text: Publicly post the provider's remaining credentials
options.rationale: Exposing credentials publicly is grossly insecure and nonsensical.

stem: Which of the following is LEAST relevant as a personnel-security control during the employee termination process?

options.text: Selecting the new marketing campaign slogan
options.rationale: Choosing a marketing slogan has nothing to do with securely terminating an employee's access and recovering assets, making it least relevant.

options.text: Revoking system access and credentials
options.rationale: Access revocation is a core, highly relevant termination control.

options.text: Recovering company assets (badge, laptop, tokens)
options.rationale: Asset recovery is a standard and relevant part of termination.

options.text: Reminding the employee of ongoing NDA obligations
options.rationale: Reinforcing continuing confidentiality obligations is a relevant termination step.
